analysis: Reviewed .github/workflows/provider-tests.yml (head lines 1-1051). The change is CI-only: it adds a 'Choose this job's Actions cache' step per job (e.g. lines 64-76, 182-194, 312-324, 795-807, 914-926, 1033-1045) that sets CI_ACTIONS_CACHE=off when a darkbloom-* runner has no DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL, and gates each cache restore/save step on env.CI_ACTIONS_CACHE != 'off' (lines 98, 140, 210, 252, 340, 382, 417, 430, 478, 515, 577, 588, 823, 865, 942, 984). It also adds a 'Discard a damaged or unsafe cached .git' step (lines 107-132 and its copies) that rejects a restored .git containing symlinks, non-sample hooks, core.fsmonitor/hooksPath/include config, or a failed fsck, which reduces cache-poisoning risk. Only pushes to master/dev save caches (SAVE_CACHES, line 39), and PRs only restore. Actions remain SHA-pinned, permissions are contents: read, and persist-credentials is false. None of this touches provider runtime, coordinator-provider protocol, attestation, App Attest, prefix-cache crypto (T-041), fan helper or hold socket. The provider-ci-build and provider-ci-products actions, scripts/ci-test-products.py and the cache restore-key behavior are outside the supplied evidence. Hooks are checked via find -ipath, and nested submodule .git contents are covered only if they live under the cached .git. The cluster-release-checks job's later steps (after line 1051) were not supplied, so cache handling there is not reviewed. Residual CI supply-chain questions: cached .git trust, and the release-bound strict_cache semantics in the unseen composite actions. No finding qualifies on the supplied evidence.
